LoginPage.title: Login
LoginPage.somethingWentWrongPleaseTryAgain: Something went wrong. Please try again.

SettingsPage.title: Settings
SettingsPage.lockedSettings: Some settings are managed via the configuration file and cannot be changed here.
SettingsPage.lockedSettingTooltip: This setting is locked because it is managed via the settings configuration file.

library.title: Library Settings
library.description: Configure your library name and web URL. These are used in for instance emails and the OPDS feed.

autoImport.title: Auto-Import
autoImport.description: Configure automatic book import from a directory
autoImport.explanation: Storyteller can be configured to automatically import book files from a specific directory. When enabled, Storyteller will set up a filesystem watcher for the directory and automatically import any new book files it finds.
autoImport.defaultImportModeDescription: How to handle files found in import directories. Individual paths can override this.

scanControls.title: Library Scanning
scanControls.description: Scan your library for new files and changes. Scans check all tracked books and import paths for additions, removals, and modified files.
scanControls.scanNote: Re-reads all import paths and book metadata, even if files haven't changed since the last scan.
scanControls.cronExpressionDescription: Standard cron syntax (minute hour day month weekday). The expression is evaluated in the server's timezone.
scanControls.metadataFieldOverridesDescription: Controls how Storyteller handles metadata from book files during scans. The default (fill empty) is suitable for most users. If you also manage your books with other tools (e.g. Calibre, Audiobookshelf) and want those changes reflected in Storyteller, consider using always override.
scanControls.showSimpleOverrides: Use a single setting for all fields

skippedImportPaths.title: Skipped import paths
skippedImportPaths.description: These file paths have been excluded from auto-import. Books at these paths will not be re-imported during scans.

readaloud.title: Readaloud
readaloud.description: Configure where new readaloud files are saved when the input files were not uploaded through the web client
readaloud.cleanCacheAfterReadaloudDescription: Automatically delete processed audio and transcription files after a readaloud is successfully created. Saves disk space, but means a full restart is needed if you want to re-align later.
readaloud.clearCacheNowDescription: Delete all processed audio and transcription files across the library now. Original files are left untouched.
readaloud.clearCacheConfirmDescription: Delete processed audio and transcription files for every book in the library? This frees disk space but means a full restart is needed to re-align books later. Original files are left untouched.

audio.title: Audio Settings
audio.maxTrackLengthDescription: Audio tracks longer than this will be split before transcribing. This can help reduce memory usage during transcription.

transcription.title: Transcription Settings
transcription.description: Configure how Storyteller transcribes audiobook narration to text. By default, transcription runs locally using whisper.cpp. You can also use paid third-party services.
transcription.whisperBuildDeprecated: cuBLAS 11.8 is no longer supported. Please update to version 12 or 13.
transcription.whisperModelDescription: The default (tiny) is sufficient for most English books. For books with many uncommon words, or in languages other than English, you may need larger models like small or medium.
transcription.whisperThreadsDescription: Change the parallelization level of the Whisper model. Can result in a massive speed increase when doing GPU-accelerated transcription.
transcription.whisperThreadsNote: It is not recommended to set both this value and the "Number of audio tracks to transcribe in parallel" value to a value greater than 1. Choose one or the other.
transcription.whisperThreadsWarning: Setting above 1 may reduce transcription accuracy but increases speed by splitting audio into chunks processed in parallel. Do not report bugs if you set this to a value greater than 1 and are not able to get a consistent Readaloud, only if you cannot get a consistent Readaloud even with a value of 1.
transcription.whisperCpuFallbackDescription: If you have a GPU variant installed but want to fall back to CPU transcription, select a CPU variant here.
transcription.whisperServerUrlDescription: e.g. http://192.168.1.19:8080 for the local whisper.cpp server.
transcription.whisperServerApiKeyDescription: Only necessary if your server requires an API key.
transcription.whisperServerDescription: Use a remote, self-hosted whisper.cpp server for transcription. Useful if you have a powerful machine to offload transcription to.
transcription.bucketNameDescription: Amazon Transcribe requires files to be uploaded to an S3 bucket before starting the transcribe job. This is the bucket Storyteller will upload files to.
transcription.baseUrlDescription: You can use a custom base URL to point at a OpenAI-compatible service like a self-hosted speaches instance or a remote whisper.cpp HTTP server.
transcription.modelNameDescription: e.g. Systran/faster-distil-whisper-large-v3 for faster-whisper-server, or whisper-1 for OpenAI Cloud.
transcription.deepgramModelDescription: Can be any model the server supports, like nova-3, nova-2, nova, enhanced, base or whisper. Defaults to nova-3.

parallelization.title: Parallelization Settings
parallelization.description: Audio transcoding is single-threaded, and Whisper has diminishing returns on multi-core processing for a single file. Since Storyteller splits input audio into multiple tracks, it can run transcoding and transcription in parallel.
parallelization.parallelTranscodesDescription: Transcoding one track will use one CPU core
parallelization.parallelTranscribesDescription: Transcribing one track will use up to 4 CPU cores (when using CPU-based transcription)
parallelization.parallelWhisperBuildDescription: Whenever the Storyteller container is recreated (e.g. after an update), it will rebuild whisper.cpp. This process can be sped up by dedicating multiple CPU cores.

sso.title: Authentication Providers
sso.description: Configure external authentication providers for single sign-on
sso.name: Name *
sso.allowRegistrationDescription: Automatically create accounts for new users from this provider.
sso.groupPermissionsDescription: Map OIDC groups to permissions. If specified, users not in any listed group will be denied access.
sso.disablePasswordLoginDescriptionEnabled: Only allow login via configured authentication providers. Most OPDS clients do not support OAuth.
sso.disablePasswordLoginDescriptionDisabled: Requires an auth provider with a group that can change server settings.

upload.title: Upload Settings
upload.description: Configure upload chunk size for large file uploads
upload.overriddenWarning: Your max chunk size is overridden via the environment variable STORYTELLER_MAX_UPLOAD_CHUNK_SIZE. Change that environment variable to change the value, or unset it to configure the value here.
upload.enableMaxChunkSizeDescription: Only enable this if you're running into maximum request size issues with your reverse proxy or hosting provider.
upload.maxChunkSizeDescription: Default is 100MB, which is Cloudflare's maximum request size.

email.title: Email Settings
email.description: Configure SMTP settings for sending emails (invitations, password resets, etc.)
email.forceTlsDescription: Disabling this option does not disable TLS. By default, Storyteller will use STARTTLS to negotiate a TLS connection. If you have this option enabled and see an error about an incorrect TLS version, try disabling it.

opds.title: OPDS Settings
opds.description: Configure the OPDS feed for your library. OPDS is a standard for publishing e-book catalogs.
opds.enabledDescription: Enable the OPDS feed for your library. This allows compatible e-book readers to browse your library and download books. You can access the OPDS feed at {url}.
opds.pageSizeDescription: The number of books per page in the OPDS feed. Default is 25.
opds.formatDescription: Which ebook edition to offer for download. Readaloud epubs include synchronized audio (media overlays) and are large, and many e-readers (e.g. Kindle, Kobo) can't use them, so you may prefer the plain ebook. An audiobook is always offered when available.
opds.urlsDescription: Storyteller supports both OPDS 1.2 and OPDS 2.0. Point your reader at either URL below. OPDS 1.2 is the most widely supported. OPDS 2.0 is the newer JSON-based format.

kobo.title: Kobo sync
kobo.description: Let a Kobo e-reader read its library from Storyteller, in the device's own reader, with nothing installed on it. Set a device up from Set up my e-reader.
kobo.enabledDescription: When on, a Kobo can be pointed at this server and shown the books on the shelf you give it. Where it stops reading syncs back here. Turning this off stops every Kobo that is set up from syncing; books already downloaded stay on the device and its Kobo store keeps working.

SetUpEreaderPage.title: Set up my e-reader
SetUpEreaderPage.optionsError: Could not load your library's readers.
SetUpEreaderPage.statusChoosing: Waiting for you to choose the e-reader...
SetUpEreaderPage.statusSettingUp: Found a {model}. Setting up its library...
SetUpEreaderPage.statusPointing: Pointing the e-reader at your library...
SetUpEreaderPage.setupError: Could not set up the library. Ask your Storyteller admin to enable Kobo sync.
SetUpEreaderPage.confirmError: Setup could not confirm the e-reader was configured. It has not been changed; please try again.
SetUpEreaderPage.doneStep1: The books appear in its own library, over Wi-Fi. Nothing to open or install.
SetUpEreaderPage.doneStep2: Tap a book to download it, and read as normal.
SetUpEreaderPage.doneStep3: Add a book to the shelf here and it turns up on the device by itself.
SetUpEreaderPage.doneStep4: Where you stop reading syncs back here, and the mobile app can pick up the same place.
SetUpEreaderPage.disabledBody: A Storyteller administrator needs to turn on Kobo sync in Settings before an e-reader can be set up here.
SetUpEreaderPage.unsupportedTitle: Use Chrome or Edge on a computer
SetUpEreaderPage.unsupportedBody: Setting up an e-reader directly needs Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge on a computer. Please open this page in one of those, on the computer you will plug the e-reader into.
SetUpEreaderPage.whoHelp: Their reading place syncs to their own account, so pick the person who reads on it.
SetUpEreaderPage.booksHelp: A shelf keeps it to just those books. The whole library puts everything within reach. You can change this later by setting the device up again.
SetUpEreaderPage.beforeStep1: Plug the e-reader into this computer with its cable.
SetUpEreaderPage.beforeStep2: If the device asks, choose to Connect so the computer can see it.
SetUpEreaderPage.whatIntro: This points a Kobo e-reader at your Storyteller library. The books show up in the device's own library, in its own reader, over Wi-Fi. Nothing is installed on the device, and nothing has to be typed on it.
SetUpEreaderPage.whatAdditive: It is additive: the e-reader keeps working with the Kobo store and any books you already bought. Setup only adds your Storyteller library alongside them, and it can be undone at any time.
SetUpEreaderPage.howLine1: Setup changes one line in the e-reader's own configuration file so it asks this server for its library. That is the entire change: no app, no launcher, no reboot.
SetUpEreaderPage.howLine2: The device points at <url></url>. This comes from your server's own settings, so each Storyteller instance points its devices at itself.
SetUpEreaderPage.howLine3: Books are converted on the way to the device so the Kobo remembers the exact place you stopped, not just the chapter. Where you stop reading syncs back to Storyteller, and the mobile app can carry on from the same place.
SetUpEreaderPage.howLine4: Requests Storyteller does not handle (the Kobo store, your account) pass straight through to Kobo, so nothing about the device's normal use changes.
SetUpEreaderPage.goodToKnow1: A shelf limits the device to just those books. Whichever you pick, the reader chooses which books to download; Storyteller only makes them available.
SetUpEreaderPage.goodToKnow2: Setting the same device up again rotates its access and lets you change who it is for or which shelf it sees. Old access stops working.
SetUpEreaderPage.goodToKnow3: While the device points here, its store traffic runs through this server, so the server needs to be reachable for the store to work on the device.
SetUpEreaderPage.revert: To return an e-reader to normal, plug it into a computer and edit <conf></conf> in the device's storage: set the <endpoint></endpoint> line back to <store></store>, then eject. Its own books and settings are never touched.

LibraryAuditPage.title: Library audit
LibraryAuditPage.heading: Library audit
LibraryAuditPage.subheading: Books an e-reader shelf shows badly: a missing, blank or tiny cover, a missing author, language or description, or a filename-like title.
LibraryAuditPage.scanning: Scanning every book's cover and metadata. This can take a moment on a large library.
LibraryAuditPage.errorBody: Something went wrong reading the library. Try rescanning.
LibraryAuditPage.allClearBody: Every book has a real cover, an author, a language, a description and a proper title.

repair.title: Repair book
repair.noMatch: No confident match found. Search by hand below, or edit the fields.
repair.nothingToApply: Nothing to apply. Fill in at least one field.

autoRepair.title: Auto-repair the library
autoRepair.description: Every flagged book is looked up on Open Library. Confident matches are listed below for you to review before anything is written. A database backup is taken first.
autoRepair.noConfident: No confident matches were found. Repair these books one at a time.
